subject: LLM data handling: subprocessor delegation and custody of prompts/responses
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aureliahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: aurelia-legal@aureliahealth.com
Date: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial DPA questions – vendor subprocessors & prompt/response custody

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aurelia’s security and legal teams reviewed the materials and have two items they flagged that we need to resolve before procurement can proceed:

1) Subprocessor delegation: our DPA requires an explicit chain-of-custody for any subprocessors that process PHI or identifiable patient data. We need a clear mapping of which Redwood subprocessors will see inference payloads for our dedicated deployment and what controls (onshore routing, KMS) are in place.

2) Prompt/response custody and training exclusions: Aurelia needs to ensure that prompts and model outputs are never used for model improvement (no-LLM-learning) unless we agree to opt in and execute an addendum. We also want clarity on whether prompt/response logs are retained in a way that would allow export to third-party model trainers.

I attached a redline of the standard DPA and a spreadsheet with the subprocessor questions. Can you route to the right ops/legal contacts at Redwood and let us know expected timelines for evidence (attestation, onshore routing proof, KMS scope)?

Appreciate it — Maria

--
Maria Lopez
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Aurelia Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions – vendor subprocessors & prompt/response custody

Maria —

Thanks for the thorough note and the attachments. I’ve looped in Laura (Head of Privacy Programs) and Priyom (Ops) who will lead the technical/evidence response. High-level answers up front so procurement can continue:

- Subprocessors & chain-of-custody: Redwood publishes an authenticated subprocessor matrix; for Dedicated deployments the processing path is configurable to onshore-only GPU hosts (we map by region). We will confirm which subprocessors touch inference telemetry vs. backup/monitoring systems and provide the matrix with role-level access.

- No-LLM-learning / custody: Redwood's hosted telemetry (default) can be enabled or disabled per account. For Dedicated and Private we support a strict ‘no-learning’ profile (no export of prompts/responses to model training stores) — we treat prompt/response logs as customer data and can provide an attestation.

Laura and Priyom — can you take point on the following deliverables for Aurelia?

1) Completed subprocessor matrix with process-level notes and onshore routing evidence (expected delivery: 5 business days)
2) No-learning attestation and short ops runbook describing retention windows, ephemeral KV handling, and export controls (expected delivery: 3 business days)
3) Example logs showing KMS-wrapped keys and region metadata (if feasible without exposing customer data)

Maria — if those timelines work I’ll open a HubSpot deal task and link the DocuSign envelope for their DPA redline.

Best,
Jonas
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:15:23 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions – vendor subprocessors & prompt/response custody

Jonas / Priyom —

I reviewed Maria’s attachments. Quick operational notes and proposed artifacts:

- Subprocessor matrix: we will produce a filtered matrix that highlights subprocessors with potential access to inference payloads (serving, observability, backups). That will include SSO/audit access owner and whether they have access to raw transcript data.

- Onshore routing evidence: provide VPC flow diagram + routing policy + a short traffic-capture snippet showing regional tag headers (redacted).

- No-learning attestation: signed statement from Privacy + Ops. Also provide the internal flag name (opt_out_model_improvement) and the code path that ensures telemetry is dropped before training buckets are populated. We can include a short pseudocode snippet in the runbook to satisfy engineers.

- Retention and export controls: clarify default retention (30 days for ephemeral prompts in ops mode) vs customer-managed retention for Dedicated (configurable to 0–90 days). Provide example API calls to purge and an explanation of how exports are gated (DocuSign/approved data pipeline only).

Attachments we'll include in our package to Aurelia:
- Redwood_subprocessors_filtered_2026-09.xlsx
- no_learning_attestation_signed.pdf
- routing_vpc_diagram_redacted.png
- ops_runbook_prompt_handling_v1.pdf

I’ll draft the attestation and runbook today; Priyom, can you pull the routing snippet and confirm the retention APIs?

Laura Bennett
Director, Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@aureliahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: aurelia-legal@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions – vendor subprocessors & prompt/response custody

Jonas/Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and proposed artifacts — the timelines look workable. A few clarifying asks before we close the loop:

- In the attestation, can you explicitly state whether any subprocessors have the right to re-identify or persistently store prompts/responses outside the customer data lifecycle? We need that language for our procurement checklist.

- For the retention API, can you provide the exact API endpoint and an example curl that removes stored prompt logs for an account? We will route that to our engineers for verification.

- Lastly, we may request an addendum that restricts derivative usage to signed opt-ins only (we'll attach that to the DPA redline). Please confirm Redwood’s standard process for opt-in addenda (signature routing + effective date mechanics).

If you can include those three clarifications in the attestation and runbook, procurement should be able to proceed next week.

Appreciate it — Maria

--
Maria Lopez
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Aurelia Health
